definition_zh: 恢复青春；恢复活力；使重新焕发生机；更新改造
definition_en: the process of making someone or something look, feel, or become young and energetic again
core_image: 一位白发老人走到泉水边，弯腰掬水入口，起身时鬓角已转黑
scene: 院角那株老槐树被砍去枯枝，剪去纠缠的根，第二年春天又抽出满树新叶。After years of careful pruning, the square showed a remarkable rejuvenation.
sceneCN: 这里 rejuvenation 是「恢复生机」（第 3 个义项：让衰老或衰退的事物重新显得年轻、有生气）；句意为经过多年的精心修剪，广场呈现出令人惊叹的生机复苏。老人饮下泉水、白发转黑，就是这个词最直观的画面。

pos.zh: 恢复青春；恢复活力；更新改造

collocations.phrase: the rejuvenation of the city centre

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀 -ation 得到的动词，义为「使恢复青春；使重新活跃」
动词的过去分词作形容词，义为「焕然一新的；重新焕发活力的」
现在分词作形容词，义为「使人恢复活力的；令人精神一振的」
加表示施动者的后缀 -or，义为「使人恢复活力的事物；焕活装置」
与 rejuvenation 共享拉丁词干 juven-，义为「青春期的状态；返老还童」

senses.title: A restored youthful appearance
senses.definition: the process by which a face or body looks young again
senses.definitionCN: 面部或身体重新显得年轻的过程
senses.example: The cream promises rejuvenation of tired skin.
senses.exampleCN: 这款面霜号称能让疲惫的肌肤重焕青春。
senses.why: Juvenis is Latin for young, so the noun at first simply names the return of a youthful look.
senses.whyCN: juvenis 在拉丁语里意为「年轻的」，所以这个词最初指的就是年轻模样的回归。

senses.title: Renewed personal energy
senses.definition: the feeling of having energy and spirit again after a dull or tiring period
senses.definitionCN: 在沉闷或疲惫的时期之后重新拥有精力与精神的感觉
senses.example: Two weeks by the sea brought a complete rejuvenation of body and mind.
senses.exampleCN: 在海边待了两周，身心都彻底焕发起来。
senses.why: Youth is not only a face but a mood, so being young again also means feeling energetic anew.
senses.whyCN: 年轻不只是脸庞的状态，也是一种心境，所以「再次年轻」也意味着重新感到精力充沛。

senses.title: Giving new life to something old
senses.definition: the process of making an old place, object, or practice lively and attractive again
senses.definitionCN: 使老旧的地方、物件或做法重新活跃、重新有吸引力的过程
senses.example: The rejuvenation of the old harbour drew new visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 旧港口的复兴吸引了新的游客。
senses.why: A building or a town can age and wear out just as a body does, so the same image transfers to places.
senses.whyCN: 建筑和城镇也会像身体一样衰老、磨损，所以同一个意象自然转移到了地方上。

senses.title: Economic revival
senses.definition: the revival of a weak industry, market, or region through fresh investment and activity
senses.definitionCN: 通过新的投资与活力使疲弱的产业、市场或地区复苏
senses.example: Cheap loans were the key to the rejuvenation of the steel industry.
senses.exampleCN: 低息贷款是这个行业振兴的关键。
senses.why: Economies are often described as tired or stagnant, and rejuvenation is the cure for that tiredness.
senses.whyCN: 经济常被形容为疲惫或停滞，而 rejuvenation 正是治好这种疲惫的良药。

senses.title: Cellular refreshment in biology
senses.titleCN: 细胞再生；生物学上的年轻化
senses.definition: the restoration of youthful function in cells, organs, or tissues
senses.definitionCN: 细胞、器官或组织恢复年轻功能的过程
senses.example: Researchers studied the rejuvenation of stem cells in older mice.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员研究了老年小鼠体内干细胞的年轻化。
senses.why: Modern biology applies the ancient image literally: tired cells are made to behave like young ones again.
senses.whyCN: 现代生物学把这个古老的意象按字面用上了：让衰老的细胞重新表现得像年轻细胞。

senses.title: Renewal of a landscape
senses.titleCN: 地貌更新；土地重获生机
senses.definition: the renewal of a landscape, river, or damaged land after care or natural processes
senses.definitionCN: 在人工管护或自然过程作用下，地貌、河流或受损土地重新焕发生机
senses.example: The rejuvenation of the river valley allowed the fish to return.
senses.exampleCN: 河谷恢复活力后，鱼群重新回来了。
senses.why: Land can look worn out, so giving it back its vigour uses the same return-to-youth metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 土地也会显得衰败，让它重获活力沿用着同样的「回归青春」比喻。

intro.en: Rejuvenation joins the Latin prefix re- (again) to juvenis (young), with the verb-forming suffix -ate and the noun-forming -ion.
intro.cn: rejuvenation 由拉丁语前缀 re-（再次）与 juvenis（年轻的）组合，再叠加动词化词缀 -ate 和名词化词缀 -ion 构成。

items.en: The root is generally reconstructed as *h₂yew-, the source of words for youth or vigour; the precise range of its earliest meanings is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为词根可重构为 *h₂yew-，是表示年轻或活力的词的来源；其最早期意义的准确范围不确定。

items.en: Iuvenis meant young, and iuventus meant youth; the stem also gave Latin iuvere, to help or please.
items.cn: iuvenis 意为「年轻的」，iuventus 意为「青春」；这个词干也产生了拉丁语 iuvere（帮助、使愉快）。

items.en: The prefix re- means again or back; re- with a young root marks a return to youth in later coinages.
items.cn: 前缀 re- 表示「再次、返回」；在后来的构词里，re- 与「年轻」词根相合就是「重返青春」。

items.en: Rejuvenatio and rejuvenare are recorded in medieval Latin before the English noun appears; the exact coinage date is uncertain.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语中先有 rejuvenatio 与 rejuvenare，之后英语名词才出现；确切造词年代不确定。

items.en: English adopts rejuvenate and rejuvenation in the nineteenth century, first in medical and general prose.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪吸收 rejuvenate 与 rejuvenation，最早见于医学与一般散文。

items.en: Modern usage covers skincare, urban renewal, biology, and economic recovery.
items.cn: 现代用法覆盖护肤、城市更新、生物学与经济复苏等领域。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same young-root stem; the near-meaning group gathers nouns of renewal and recovery.
note.cn: 形近组收集同一「年轻」词干的词族；近义组收集表示更新与恢复的名词。

entries.definition: to make someone or something young or lively again.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使恢复青春、使重新有活力」；去掉了名词后缀 -ion。

entries.definition: Made to look or feel young again.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「焕然一新的、重新焕发活力的」。

entries.definition: Young, or designed for young people.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「少年的、幼稚的」；与 rejuvenation 共享拉丁语 juven- 词干。

entries.definition: The state of being young or growing young again.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「青春期的状态、返老还童」；源自同一拉丁语词干 juven-。

entries.definition: A rarer synonym meaning a return to youthful vigour.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，较罕见的同义形式，义为「重新变得年轻、恢复活力」。

entries.definition: A return to life, activity, or popularity.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「复活、复兴」；重在重新活跃，而不强调「变年轻」。

entries.definition: The act of making something new or effective again.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「更新、重新开始」；偏重使事物重新有效。

entries.definition: The process of growing or being built up again after damage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「再生、重建」；侧重从损坏中重新生长。

entries.definition: The act of bringing something back to an earlier good condition.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「修复、恢复」；强调回到原来的良好状态。

normalIntro.en: In rejuvenation, the Latin prefix re- (again) sits in front of juvenis (young), so the word literally spells out becoming young once more.
normalIntro.cn: 在 rejuvenation 里，拉丁语前缀 re-（再次）就坐在 juvenis（年轻的）前面，所以这个词字面上就是「再一次变得年轻」。

normal.en: Re- means again, juven- means young: the whole word is young again.
normal.cn: re- 表示「再次」，juven- 表示「年轻的」：整个词就是「再次年轻」。

normal.en: The -ation ending marks a noun, so rejuvenation is the process or result, not the action itself.
normal.cn: -ation 词尾标明是名词，所以 rejuvenation 指过程或结果，而不是那个动作本身。

normal.en: Juvenile, juvenescence and rejuvenation all share juven-, so any word about youth is family.
normal.cn: juvenile、juvenescence 与 rejuvenation 都共享 juven-，凡是讲「年轻」的词都是一家人。

normal.en: The verb pair is rejuvenate and rejuvenated, as in a rejuvenated city centre.
normal.cn: 动词对是 rejuvenate 与 rejuvenated，例如 rejuvenated city centre 表示焕然一新的市中心。

normal.en: Compare renewal (making new) with rejuvenation (making young): the first is about freshness, the second about youth.
normal.cn: 对比 renewal（使变新）与 rejuvenation（使变年轻）：前者讲「新」，后者讲「年轻」。

abstract.en: Picture the old man dipping water from a spring and walking away with dark hair and bright eyes.
abstract.cn: 想象老人从泉水里掬水喝下，走开时已是一头黑发、目光清亮。

abstract.en: Picture a dried sponge dropped into water and swelling back to full size.
abstract.cn: 想象一块干海绵落进水里，又胀回原来的大小。

abstract.en: Picture a faded street of shuttered shops, then the shutters lifting and lights coming on.
abstract.cn: 想象一条卷帘门紧闭的旧街，卷帘门升起、灯光亮起的那一刻。

examples.en: The rejuvenation of the town began with a new library and a repaired quay.
examples.cn: 小镇的复兴从一座新图书馆和一道修好的码头开始。

examples.en: Scientists are studying the rejuvenation of damaged tissue.
examples.cn: 科学家正在研究受损组织的年轻化。

examples.en: After the holiday she felt a real rejuvenation of spirit.
examples.cn: 度假之后，她感到精神状态真正焕然一新。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞珠内申」——想象老人喝下一颗瑞珠，身子骨一下回到申时（少年时），这就是返老还童。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再次）+ juvenis（年轻的）→ 中世纪拉丁语 rejuvenare（使年轻）与 rejuvenatio（焕新）→ 英语 rejuvenation，「再次变得年轻」。

sensesIntro.en: The noun starts with a face that looks young again, rises to renewed energy, then spreads to places, economies, cells and landscapes that are brought back to life.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从「重新显得年轻的面孔」出发，上升到「重新拥有精力」，再扩展到被重新激活的地方、经济、细胞与地貌。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old man drinks from a spring and his white hair turns black.
core.cn: 核心意象：老人饮下泉水，白发转黑。

branches.en: The face is the most literal place for youth to return.
branches.cn: 面孔是「青春回归」最字面的地方。

branches.en: Body and mind recover together after rest or travel.
branches.cn: 休息或旅行之后，身心一起恢复。

branches.en: Buildings and economies are given the youth they had lost.
branches.cn: 建筑与经济被重新赋予失去的活力。

branches.en: Cells are made to act young again in living tissue.
branches.cn: 在活体组织中，细胞被重新调回年轻状态。

branches.en: Places and landscapes both wear out and both can be brought back.
branches.cn: 地方与地貌都会衰败，也都能够被唤醒。

intro.en: Rejuvenation is built from a Latin prefix, a young-root stem, and two English suffixes, with verb and adjective relatives around it.
intro.cn: rejuvenation 由一个拉丁语前缀、一个「年轻」词根与两个英语后缀构成，周围还有动词与形容词同族。

latinIntro.en: Latin re- means again, iuvenis means young, and the stem also yields iuventus (youth) and iuvenile.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 re- 表示「再次」，iuvenis 表示「年轻的」，同一词干还产生 iuventus（青春）与 iuvenile 一系。

items.example: The prefix marks a return to youth.
items.exampleCN: 前缀标记「重返青春」。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of youth.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供「年轻」的概念。

items.example: The Latin word gives juvenile and rejuvenate.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁词衍生出 juvenile 与 rejuvenate。

items.example: It forms rejuvenate.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 rejuvenate。

items.example: It turns rejuvenate into rejuvenation.
items.exampleCN: 它把 rejuvenate 变成 rejuvenation。

items.meaning: a person or thing that acts
items.example: It forms rejuvenator.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 rejuvenator。

items.example: Juvenile shares the young root.
items.exampleCN: juvenile 共享「年轻」词根。

items.example: The stem also forms this noun.
items.exampleCN: 同一词干也构成这个名词。

items.example: It forms juvenescence.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 juvenescence。

items.example: The participle serves as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词也可作形容词。

definition_zh: 重新点燃；使（感情、兴趣、希望）重新燃起；重振
definition_en: to make a fire burn again, or to make a feeling, interest, or idea strong again after it has faded
core_image: 一堆将灭的炭灰上，有人俯身吹气，一小片橙红重新亮成火苗
scene: 两位老友在街边咖啡馆重逢，聊起少年时一起看过的球赛，眼睛里渐渐有了光。Old letters can rekindle love long after the first meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 rekindle 是「重新点燃」（第 1 个义项：让原本熄灭或快要熄灭的感情再次燃起）；句意为旧信件能在初次相识很久之后重新点燃爱意。炭灰上吹出的那一小簇火苗，就是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 重新点燃；使重新燃起；重振

collocations.zh: 重新唤起对科学的兴趣
重新引发关于该计划的争论

derivatives.zh: 去掉前缀 re- 得到的动词，义为「点燃；激起」
过去分词作形容词，义为「重新燃起的；被重新激起的」
与 rekindle 共享 kindle 词根，义为「引火物；小木柴」

senses.title: To make a feeling burn again
senses.definition: to make love, affection, or passion strong again after it has faded
senses.definitionCN: 在感情、爱意或热情冷却之后使其重新强烈起来
senses.example: A shared song rekindled their affection.
senses.exampleCN: 一首共同的歌重新点燃了他们的感情。
senses.why: Kindle comes from an old word for a candle, and a feeling is pictured as a light that can go out and then be lit once more.
senses.whyCN: kindle 源自一个表示「蜡烛」的古词，感情被想象成可以熄灭、也可以被重新点亮的光。

senses.title: To light a fire again
senses.definition: to set a fire, a candle, or glowing coals burning again
senses.definitionCN: 让火、蜡烛或余烬重新燃烧
senses.example: He rekindled the stove with a handful of dry twigs.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一把干树枝把炉火重新点着了。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most literal sense, the fire that died and then flares up again.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老、最字面的义项：已经熄灭的火又烧了起来。

senses.title: To bring back interest
senses.definition: to make someone interested in something again after a pause
senses.definitionCN: 在中断之后让人重新对某事物产生兴趣
senses.example: A school visit rekindled her interest in history.
senses.exampleCN: 一次学校参观重新激起了她对历史的兴趣。
senses.why: Interest behaves like a fire: it can dwindle to a spark and then be fanned back to strength.
senses.whyCN: 兴趣就像火：它可以缩成一点火星，再被重新扇旺。

senses.title: To restore hope
senses.definition: to make hope strong again when people had almost given up
senses.definitionCN: 在人们几乎要放弃时让希望重新变得强烈
senses.example: The rescue rekindled hope across the town.
senses.exampleCN: 这次营救让整个小镇重燃希望。
senses.why: Hope is one of the most common fires in language, often described as flickering or dying before it is renewed.
senses.whyCN: 希望是语言中最常见的「火」之一，常被说成摇曳将熄，之后又被重新点亮。

senses.title: To restart a debate or conflict
senses.definition: to cause an argument, debate, or conflict to begin again
senses.definitionCN: 使争论、辩论或冲突再次开始
senses.example: The new report rekindled the old argument about costs.
senses.exampleCN: 这份新报告重新引燃了关于成本的旧争论。
senses.why: Arguments can burn and be smothered; to rekindle one is to give the old heat fresh fuel.
senses.whyCN: 争论也会燃烧、也会被压灭，重新引燃就是给旧火添上新柴。

intro.en: Rekindle is the English prefix re- (again) added to kindle, which goes back to an Old Norse word for lighting a candle or a fire.
intro.cn: rekindle 是英语前缀 re-（再次）加在 kindle 上，而 kindle 可追溯到古诺尔斯语中表示「点燃蜡烛或火」的词。

items.en: The deeper root of kindle is generally connected with a word for burning or shining; the exact reconstructed form is uncertain.
items.cn: kindle 更早的词根一般认为与表示「燃烧、发光」的词有关；确切的重构形式不确定。

items.en: Old Norse kynda meant to set fire to or light, and kynna meant a torch: the fire image is native.
items.cn: 古诺尔斯语 kynda 意为「点燃、焚烧」，kynna 意为「火把」：火的意象来自本族。

items.en: Kindle appears in Middle English, first of a real flame and then of feeling; its earliest date is uncertain.
items.cn: kindle 在中古英语中出现，先指真实的火焰，后来指情感；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The prefixed form rekindle appears in English by the fourteenth century, used of lamps and fires.
items.cn: 加前缀的 rekindle 至十四世纪已见于英语，用于灯与火。

items.en: Modern usage extends the verb to feelings, interest, hope, friendship and public debate.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个动词扩展到感情、兴趣、希望、友谊与公共争论。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the kindle family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of lighting, renewing, and stirring up.
note.cn: 形近组收集 kindle 词族；近义组收集表示点火、更新与激起情绪的动词。

entries.definition: To start a fire or to stir up a feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「点燃、激起」；去掉前缀 re- 就是它的基础形式。

entries.definition: Small dry pieces of wood used to start a fire.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「引火物、小木柴」；与 rekindle 共享 kindle 词根。

entries.definition: An oven for baking or drying materials.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「窑」；只是拼写相近，词源不同，与 kindle 并无关系。

entries.definition: To make someone remember something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「提醒、使想起」；只是与 re- 前缀相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To bring something back to life, use, or popularity.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使复活、使复兴」；侧重重新有生命力。

entries.definition: To set a lamp, a candle, or a fire burning again.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「重新点燃（灯、蜡烛或火）」；比 rekindle 更偏具体物体。

entries.definition: To give fresh strength or vigour to something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使更新、使恢复精力」；不强调火焰意象。

entries.definition: To make something begin to burn.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「点燃、使燃烧」；只指起始点火，不含「再次」的含义。

normalIntro.en: Rekindle is re- (again) plus kindle (to light), so its meaning is simply to light again, whether a fire or a feeling.
normalIntro.cn: rekindle 就是 re-（再次）加 kindle（点燃），意思很直接：重新点起来，无论点的是火还是感情。

normal.en: Kindle is an old fire word, so rekindle means lighting the same flame once more.
normal.cn: kindle 是一个古老的「火」词，所以 rekindle 就是把同一簇火再点一次。

normal.en: The prefix re- in English nearly always signals doing something a second time.
normal.cn: 英语里的前缀 re- 几乎总表示「第二次做某事」。

normal.en: Kindling is the dry twig you use to start a fire and rekindle a dull hearth.
normal.cn: kindling 是点火用的干树枝，也是重新点燃冷炉子时用的东西。

normal.en: Watch the final -le: the word is rekindle, not rekindal or rekindel.
normal.cn: 注意结尾的 -le：拼写是 rekindle，而不是 rekindal 或 rekindel。

normal.en: Compare ignite (fire starts for the first time) with rekindle (a fire comes back).
normal.cn: 对比 ignite（第一次点着）与 rekindle（火又回来了）。

abstract.en: Picture two people on a park bench laughing at an old joke, the warmth coming back into the evening.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人坐在公园长椅上为旧笑话大笑，那股暖意又回到了傍晚的空气里。

abstract.en: Picture grey ash in a stove, then a breath, then one orange spark.
abstract.cn: 想象炉膛里一堆灰烬，然后一口吹气，然后一点橙红色的火星。

abstract.en: Picture a bookshop where the lights come back on one lamp at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一家书店里的灯一盏一盏重新亮起来。

examples.en: The reunion rekindled an old friendship that had faded after school.
examples.cn: 这次重逢重新点燃了毕业后渐渐淡去的旧友谊。

examples.en: A single wet match is enough to rekindle a heap of dry leaves.
examples.cn: 一根湿火柴就足以重新引燃一堆干树叶。

examples.en: His lecture rekindled public interest in the old language.
examples.cn: 他的讲座重新激起了公众对这门古老语言的兴趣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞肯逗」——瑞气来肯把火逗一逗，将灭的炉子就又旺了，就像感情被重新逗热。

root: 古诺尔斯语 kynda（点燃）→ 中古英语 kindle（点燃；激起）→ 加前缀 re-（再次）→ 英语 rekindle，「重新点着」。

sensesIntro.en: The verb begins with a feeling that glows again, drops to the literal fire it came from, then extends to interest, hope, and public conflict.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词先从「重新发光的感情」说起，回到它本来的字面火，再扩展到兴趣、希望与公共冲突。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a breath on grey coals and one orange flame flares up.
core.cn: 核心意象：对着灰烬吹一口气，一簇橙色火苗窜起。

branches.en: Love and affection return like warmth to a cold hearth.
branches.cn: 爱与亲情像暖意回到冷炉膛一样回来。

branches.en: The literal fire is where the whole family of meanings began.
branches.cn: 字面上的火是这一整族意义的起点。

branches.en: Interest and hope are lights that can be snuffed and then fanned back.
branches.cn: 兴趣与希望是可以被吹灭、也能被扇旺的灯。

branches.en: Shared songs and school visits are both sparks that start the same warmth again.
branches.cn: 共同的歌曲和学校参观都是重新燃起同一份暖意的火星。

branches.en: Debate and conflict are old fires given fresh fuel.
branches.cn: 争论与冲突是被重新添柴的旧火。

intro.en: Rekindle is a rare English word with a Norse fire root, wrapped in the productive prefix re- that marks repetition.
intro.cn: rekindle 是少数带有北欧语「火」词根的英语词，外面包着表示重复的高产前缀 re-。

latinIntro.en: Rekindle has no Latin ancestry: its fire-word comes from Old Norse, and only the prefix re- is Latin in origin.
latinIntro.cn: rekindle 没有拉丁语血统：它的「火」词来自古诺尔斯语，只有前缀 re- 源自拉丁语。

items.example: The prefix marks a second lighting.
items.exampleCN: 前缀标记「第二次点燃」。

items.meaning: to set fire to, to light
items.example: It is the remote ancestor of kindle.
items.exampleCN: 它是 kindle 的远祖。

items.meaning: to light a fire, to stir up
items.example: Kindle is the base verb.
items.exampleCN: kindle 是基础动词。

items.meaning: small wood for starting a fire
items.example: The -ing form names the material.
items.exampleCN: 带 -ing 的形式指这种材料。

items.example: The participle works as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词可作形容词。

items.example: The gerund names the act.
items.exampleCN: 动名词形式指这个动作。

items.example: The -le ending is old and only partly regular.
items.exampleCN: 结尾的 -le 十分古老，规律性有限。

items.example: Kiln only looks new, it is an old homely word.
items.exampleCN: kiln 只是看起像新词，其实是古老的本族词。

definition_zh: 放松；休息；消遣；（限制的）放宽；松弛
definition_en: the feeling of being calm and free from worry or effort, or the act of making a rule or rule-controlled system less strict
core_image: 一根绷紧的橡皮筋被慢慢松开，从笔直变得柔软垂落
scene: 周末午后，雨声敲着窗，沙发的人把书一合，长长地舒了一口气，肩膀整个沉了下去。Deep breathing is the simplest form of relaxation before an exam.
sceneCN: 这里 relaxation 是「放松」（第 1 个义项：紧张或疲惫之后身心松弛、不再绷着的状态）；句意为考前最简便的放松方式就是深呼吸。橡皮筋被松开后垂下，就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀 -ation 得到的动词，义为「放松；放宽」
动词的过去分词作形容词，义为「放松的；从容的；宽松的」
现在分词作形容词，义为「令人放松的」
加后缀 -ant 构成，义为「松弛剂」；形容词义为「使松弛的」

senses.title: The state of being at ease
senses.definition: the condition of being calm and free from tension or strain
senses.definitionCN: 平静而不再紧绷、不再吃力的状态
senses.example: A warm bath brings deep relaxation after a long day.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的一天之后，洗个热水澡能带来彻底的放松。
senses.why: The Latin verb relaxare means to loosen, so relaxation is the loosening of a body or mind that was held tight.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 relaxare 意为「放松、松开」，所以 relaxation 就是原本绷紧的身心松开来。

senses.title: Time spent resting
senses.definition: rest or pleasant activity that people do to recover their energy
senses.definitionCN: 人们为了恢复精力而进行的休息或愉快活动
senses.example: Reading is his favourite form of relaxation at weekends.
senses.exampleCN: 周末读书是他最喜欢的消遣方式。
senses.why: The state of being loose is also the time you spend getting loose, so the noun shifts from state to activity.
senses.whyCN: 「松下来」的状态也就是你花在「放松下来」上的时间，于是名词从状态转指活动。

senses.title: A lessening of a rule
senses.definition: the act of making a rule, limit, or control less strict
senses.definitionCN: 使规定、限制或管控变得不那么严格的行为
senses.example: The relaxation of the visa rules helped the tourism industry.
senses.exampleCN: 签证规定的放宽帮助了旅游业。
senses.why: A rule is a taut rope holding people in; to relax it is literally to let the rope slacken.
senses.whyCN: 规定像一根把人们捆住的紧绷绳索，放宽规定就是把这根绳索真的放松。

senses.title: An easing of tension
senses.definition: the reduction of tension between countries, groups, or people
senses.definitionCN: 国家、群体或人与人之间紧张关系减轻
senses.example: The talks led to a relaxation of tension along the border.
senses.exampleCN: 会谈使边境沿线的紧张局势有所缓和。
senses.why: Tension is the same tightness at a larger scale, and easing it uses the same image of slackening.
senses.whyCN: 紧张在更大尺度上就是同一种「绑紧」，缓和它用的是同一个「松开」的意象。

senses.title: Physical looseness
senses.definition: the slackening of a muscle, a joint, or the walls of a vessel
senses.definitionCN: 肌肉、关节或血管壁变得松弛
senses.example: The drug causes relaxation of the blood vessels.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药物会使血管松弛。
senses.why: This restores the original Latin sense of loosening a tight physical thing, applied to the body.
senses.whyCN: 这里回到拉丁语最原始的意思：把物理上绷紧的东西松开，用在了身体上。

senses.title: Mathematical slackness
senses.titleCN: 数学中的松弛（放宽条件）
senses.definition: the replacement of a strict condition in a problem by a weaker one
senses.definitionCN: 在问题中用一个较弱的条件替换严格条件
senses.example: The relaxation of the problem made an exact solution possible.
senses.exampleCN: 对问题条件的放宽使得精确求解成为可能。
senses.why: A constraint is a tight binding; relaxing it loosens the requirement, so the metaphor works in mathematics too.
senses.whyCN: 约束就像一道紧绷的束带，放宽约束就是松开要求，所以这个比喻在数学里同样成立。

intro.en: Relaxation comes from Latin relaxatio, a loosening, built on the verb relaxare: re- (back) plus laxus (loose).
intro.cn: relaxation 来自拉丁语 relaxatio（松解），建立在动词 relaxare 之上：re-（向后）加 laxus（松的）。

items.en: Laxus has no firm single reconstruction; it is generally linked with words for slack or weak, but the exact form is uncertain.
items.cn: laxus 没有可靠的单一重构形式；一般认为它与表示「松弛、虚弱」的词有关，但确切形式不确定。

items.en: Laxus meant loose, slack, or wide, and laxare meant to loosen or open out.
items.cn: laxus 意为「松的、松弛的、宽的」，laxare 意为「松开、展开」。

items.en: The prefix re- (back) joined laxare to make relaxare, to loosen back or stretch out.
items.cn: 前缀 re-（向后）加在 laxare 上构成 relaxare，意为「松开、伸展开」。

items.en: The noun relaxatio named the act of loosening, first of ropes, limbs, and later of minds.
items.cn: 名词 relaxatio 指「松开」的动作，先用于绳索、肢体，后来用于心神。

items.en: English relaxation enters through French and Latin in the late Middle Ages; the earliest date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 relaxation 在中世纪后期经法语和拉丁语进入英语；确切年代不确定。

items.en: Modern usage covers rest, leisure, medical slackening, and the easing of rules.
items.cn: 现代用法覆盖休息、休闲、医学上的松弛以及规定的放宽。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin lax- stem; the near-meaning group gathers nouns of rest and of loosening.
note.cn: 形近组收集拉丁语 lax- 词干的词族；近义组收集表示休息与松开的近义名词。

entries.definition: To become less tense, or to make a rule less strict.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「放松、放宽」；去掉名词后缀 -ation 就是它的基础形式。

entries.definition: Calm and not worried, or not strict.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「放松的、从容的、宽松的」；由过去分词构成。

entries.definition: Not strict or not tightly controlled.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不严格的、松懈的」；与 relaxation 共享拉丁语 laxus 词根。

entries.definition: A drug or substance that makes muscles relax.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「松弛剂」；形容词义为「使松弛的」。

entries.definition: A period of not working or moving.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「休息、歇息」；偏重停止劳作，不一定指身心松弛。

entries.definition: Free time when you can do what you enjoy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「空闲、闲暇」；强调可以自由支配的时间。

entries.definition: The act of making pain or a rule less strict.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缓解、放宽」；与 relaxation 的放宽义接近。

entries.definition: A quiet and peaceful state without worry.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「平静、镇定」；侧重情绪上的安然。

normalIntro.en: Relaxation is the noun behind relax: sit re- plus lax together and you get exactly what the word means, a loosening.
normalIntro.cn: relaxation 是 relax 背后的名词：把 re- 和 lax 放一起，得到的就是这个词的字面意思——松开。

normal.en: lax means loose in Latin, so any relax- word is about something no longer being tight.
normal.cn: lax 在拉丁语里意为「松的」，所以凡是 relax- 系列的词都与「不再绷紧」有关。

normal.en: The -ation ending makes it a noun: relaxation is the state or act of getting loose.
normal.cn: -ation 词尾使它成为名词：relaxation 就是「松开」的状态或动作。

normal.en: Lax, relax, relaxed, relaxation and relaxant all share the same three letters, lax.
normal.cn: lax、relax、relaxed、relaxation 与 relaxant 都共享同样三个字母 lax。

normal.en: A relaxation of the rules is the same loosening, applied to a sentence-like constraint.
normal.cn: a relaxation of the rules 表达的仍是同一种松开，只是用在规定这类约束上。

normal.en: Compare resting (stopping work) with relaxation (letting the muscles go slack even while learning).
normal.cn: 对比 resting（停止工作）与 relaxation（哪怕在学习时也让肌肉松下来）。

abstract.en: Picture a rubber band pulled tight between two fingers, then gently released until it hangs soft.
abstract.cn: 想象橡皮筋被两根手指拉得笔直，然后轻轻松开，直到它柔软地垂下来。

abstract.en: Picture a clenched fist slowly opening, palm up, and the palm becoming warm.
abstract.cn: 想象一只紧握的拳头慢慢张开、掌心朝上，掌心渐渐有了温度。

abstract.en: Picture a guard lowering a raised gate an inch at a time so carts can pass.
abstract.cn: 想象守卫把抬起的横杆一点点放低，让车辆能够过去。

examples.en: Yoga classes teach relaxation as well as strength.
examples.cn: 瑜伽课程既教力量，也教放松。

examples.en: The government announced a relaxation of import limits.
examples.cn: 政府宣布放宽进口限额。

examples.en: She sees gardening as her only true relaxation.
examples.cn: 她把园艺看作自己唯一真正的放松方式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞拉克森」——瑞气一来、拉克一松，森森树影下打个盹，整个人就松开了。

root: 拉丁语 re-（向后）+ laxus（松的）→ laxare（松开）→ relaxare（放松、伸展）→ relaxatio → 英语 relaxation，核心义「把绷紧之物松开」。

sensesIntro.en: The noun begins with a body and mind that stop straining, moves into the free time spent that way, then turns back to its Latin job of loosening rules, tensions, muscles and constraints.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从「身心不再紧绷」开始，转而指这样度过的空闲时光，最后回到拉丁语的本来工作：松开规定、紧张、肌肉与约束。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tight rubber band is slowly let go until it hangs soft.
core.cn: 核心意象：绷紧的橡皮筋被慢慢松开，柔软地垂下。

branches.en: The first sense is the calm body and mind after strain.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是疲惫之后平静松弛的身心。

branches.en: The second sense is the leisure you spend getting loose.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是花在「松下来」上的闲适时光。

branches.en: Rules and tensions are ropes that are allowed to slacken.
branches.cn: 规定与紧张都是被允许松下来的绳索。

branches.en: Both personal calm and official leniency are the same loosening.
branches.cn: 个人的平静与官方的宽松是同一种松开。

branches.en: Muscles and mathematical conditions both go from tight to slack.
branches.cn: 肌肉与数学条件都从「紧」变成「松」。

intro.en: Relaxation is a Latin stem lax- (loose) with a returning prefix and two suffixes; lax, relax, and relaxant share it.
intro.cn: relaxation 是拉丁语词干 lax-（松的）加上一个「返回」前缀与两个后缀；lax、relax 与 relaxant 都与之同源。

latinIntro.en: Latin laxus means loose and laxare means to loosen; relaxare adds the prefix re- to give a stretching back or out.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 laxus 意为「松的」，laxare 意为「松开」；relaxare 再加上前缀 re-，表示「向后或向外伸展」。

items.example: The prefix shows a pulling back into slack.
items.exampleCN: 前缀表示往回拉到松弛状态。

items.example: The root gives the whole family its looseness.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根给整个词族「松开」的含义。

items.example: The adjective also gives English lax.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词也给出英语的 lax。

items.example: It is the direct source of relax.
items.exampleCN: 它是 relax 的直接来源。

items.example: It forms the verb relax.
items.exampleCN: 它构成动词 relax。

items.example: It forms relaxation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 relaxation。

items.example: It forms relaxant.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 relaxant。

items.example: Lax keeps the bare root meaning.
items.exampleCN: lax 保留了词根本义。

items.example: Relax lost the -are ending of its Latin source.
items.exampleCN: relax 丢掉了拉丁语来源的 -are 词尾。

items.example: A muscle relaxant is a common medical noun.
items.exampleCN: muscle relaxant（肌肉松弛剂）是常见的医学术语。

definition_zh: 接力传递；转播；中继；接班的人；接力赛
definition_en: to pass something along from one person, place, or device to the next; a race or team in which each runner covers one stage; a device or person that receives and sends on a signal
core_image: 一只手把接力棒递到下一只手里，接着往前传
scene: 四个学生依次接力读完同一份稿子。Four students each read a section and relay the draft to the next speaker.
sceneCN: 这里 relay 是「依次传递」的意思（第 1 个义项：把东西一段一段交下去）；句意：四个学生各读一部分，再把稿子传给下一位。

pos.zh: 接力赛；替班的人；中继设备

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成动名词，义为「中继；接力传递」
relay 加 -man 构成的复合词，旧时指电报中继员

senses.title: To pass something along in stages
senses.definition: to pass a message, object, or piece of information from one person or place to the next
senses.definitionCN: 把消息、物件或信息从一个人或一个地点传到下一个
senses.example: She relayed the instructions to the rest of the team.
senses.exampleCN: 她把指令转达给了团队其他成员。
senses.why: The original sense is a fresh set of horses or riders waiting to take over, so the word always means hand over the load and let someone else carry it on.
senses.whyCN: 本义是等候接力的新马或新骑手；因此这个词天生含有「把负担交出去、由下一手持续」的画面，凡物只要一段一段往下传，都可用它。

senses.title: A race run in parts
senses.definition: a sporting event in which each member of a team covers one section of the course in turn
senses.definitionCN: 一种比赛项目，队中每人依次跑完赛程的一段
senses.example: Our class won the four-by-one-hundred relay.
senses.exampleCN: 我们班赢得了一百米接力赛。
senses.why: From handing over a load it is a short step to handing over a baton, and the race is simply the sport built on that handover.
senses.whyCN: 由「交负载」自然过渡到「交接力棒」，而接力赛正是把这种交接变成比赛规则的运动，义项因此从传递动作长成一个赛事名称。

senses.title: A team member replacing another
senses.definition: a person or group who take over a task from another so that the work continues without a gap
senses.definitionCN: 接替他人继续工作、使工作不中断的人或小组
senses.example: Workers dug through the night in relays of four hours.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们以四小时一班轮流彻夜挖掘。
senses.why: If horses took turns, then people can take turns too, and the word names anyone who steps in when the previous carrier stops.
senses.whyCN: 既然是马轮流接班，人当然也可以轮流；当上一棒停下、下一棒顶上时，那个顶替的人就被称为 relay，强调的仍是「不间断」。

senses.title: A device that forwards a signal
senses.definition: an electrical or electronic device that receives a weak signal and sends it on with new power
senses.definitionCN: 接收微弱信号并重新放大后发出的电气或电子装置
senses.example: The satellite relay carried the call across the ocean.
senses.exampleCN: 那颗卫星中继把通话传过了大洋。
senses.why: A station of fresh horses revived a tired messenger, so a device that refreshes a fading signal wears the same name.
senses.whyCN: 新马驿站让疲惫的送信人重新有力，同理，把逐渐衰弱的信号接收、增强再发出的装置，也借用了「换一程」的意象。

senses.title: To broadcast a received programme
senses.definition: to receive a radio or television signal and send it out again to other audiences
senses.definitionCN: 接收广播或电视信号后，再向其他观众发送出去
senses.example: The station relays the concert to listeners in remote villages.
senses.exampleCN: 这家电台把音乐会转播给偏远村庄的听众。
senses.why: A signal passed from one transmitter to another is still being handed on down the line, and broadcasting adopted the old relay idea.
senses.whyCN: 信号从一座发射台传到另一座，本质上仍是沿线路一级级往下交，广播业于是沿用旧的接力一词，专指接收后再转发出去的节目。

intro.en: Relay comes from Old French relai, a set of fresh horses kept ready to replace tired ones, from the verb relaier, to leave behind and get new ones.
intro.cn: relay 源自古法语 relai，指备好用来替换疲劳马匹的一批新马，动词为 relaier，意为「留下旧的、换上新的」。

items.en: Relai names a supply of fresh horses waiting at a post station.
items.cn: relai 指驿站里预备好的一批新马。

items.en: The word enters English for riders who take over the journey.
items.cn: 该词进入英语，指接手继续赶路的骑手。

items.en: Hunting and animal keeping use it for a fresh pack of hounds or a spare team.
items.cn: 狩猎与养畜中用它指新换的一群猎犬或备用牲口。

items.en: Telegraphy turns the human handover into a technical relay that boosts a signal.
items.cn: 十九世纪电报技术把人力接班变成能增强信号的技术中继。

items.en: Sport, broadcasting, and computing give relays to races, programmes, and networks.
items.cn: 现代英语把 relay 延伸到体育接力、节目转播和电脑网络。

note.en: Relay is about handover, so it sits beside release and delay in form and beside hand on and broadcast in meaning.
note.cn: relay 的核心是交棒，形上与 release、delay 相近，意义上的邻居则是 hand on 与 broadcast 一类词。

entries.definition: to let someone or something go free
entries.definitionCN: 释放；放开。只是拼写相近，词源不同：release 来自 relaxare，与 relay 无关。

entries.definition: to make something happen later than planned
entries.definitionCN: 推迟；耽误。只是拼写相近，词源不同：delay 来自古法语 delaier。

entries.definition: past tense of relay when it means to lay something again
entries.definitionCN: 把某物重新铺放的过去式。拼写与 relayed 相近但拼法不同，它来自前缀 re- 加 lay。

entries.definition: to send a signal or message from one place to another
entries.definitionCN: 传送；播送；发送信号

entries.definition: to send out a programme to many listeners or viewers
entries.definitionCN: 广播；播送节目

entries.definition: the act of passing something or responsibility to someone else
entries.definitionCN: 移交；交接

normalIntro.en: Relay is the horse-post word: something tired is replaced so that the journey never stops.
normalIntro.cn: relay 是驿马换班的词：旧的一停，新的一上，路程因此不中断。

normal.en: Relay a message means carry it on to the next person.
normal.cn: relay a message 就是把消息接着传给下一个人。

normal.en: Relayed keeps the same spelling for past and participle.
normal.cn: relayed 的过去式和过去分词同形，都写成 relayed。

normal.en: A relay race is decided by the handover of the baton.
normal.cn: 接力赛成败取决于交接力棒的那一下。

normal.en: In relays means in turns, one group after another.
normal.cn: in relays 表示分批轮流、一组接一组地做。

normal.en: Compare transmit: relay stresses the next link, transmit stresses the sending device.
normal.cn: 对比 transmit：relay 强调交给下一站，transmit 强调发送设备本身。

abstract.en: Picture a baton leaving one open hand and landing in another.
abstract.cn: 想象接力棒离开一只张开的手，落进另一只手里。

abstract.en: See a line of legs on the running track, each pair doing one lap.
abstract.cn: 想象跑道上排开的双腿，每一双只跑一圈。

abstract.en: Imagine a lamp on a hill that catches a signal and shines it on.
abstract.cn: 想象山岗上的一盏灯接住信号，再把它照向远方。

examples.en: He relayed the news to his parents as soon as he arrived.
examples.cn: 他一到就把消息转告给了父母。

examples.en: She ran the last leg of the relay and crossed the line first.
examples.cn: 她跑接力赛的最后一棒，第一个冲过终点。

examples.en: The hilltop tower was used to relay signals between the two towns.
examples.cn: 山顶的塔被用来在两镇之间中继信号。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞雷」——瑞雪般的雷声一棒一棒滚过山谷，声音一路传下去，就是 relay 的传递与中继；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 relai（备换的新马）← relaier（留下旧马、换上新马）；核心义为「换一程、接着传」，后世由驿马接力的画面延伸出比赛、替班、信号中继与节目转播。

sensesIntro.en: Relay starts as a handover of the load, then names the race built on it, the person who takes over, the device that refreshes a signal, and the broadcast sent on again.
sensesIntro.cn: relay 先指把负载交给下一程，再指由这种交接构成的比赛、以接替方式工作的人、把信号重新发出的设备，以及接收后再播出的节目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a baton passed from one open hand to the next.
core.cn: 核心意象：接力棒从一只手交到下一只手里。

branches.en: Passing a message on is the everyday form of the handover.
branches.cn: 把消息往下传是交接最基本的日常形态。

branches.en: A race turns the handover into rules and timing.
branches.cn: 接力赛把交接变成规则与计时。

branches.en: A person who steps in keeps the work going past the last carrier.
branches.cn: 接班的人让工作在上一棒之后继续。

branches.en: Machines and stations take over the handover once hands are no longer fast enough.
branches.cn: 当双手已不够快时，机器与电台接替了这场交接。

branches.en: Both a message and a shift depend on nobody dropping the load.
branches.cn: 传递消息与轮班干活一样，都怕中途掉棒。

intro.en: Relay has no live affix for learners, but the re- of the Old French verb is worth noticing as a hint of doing something again with a new set.
intro.cn: relay 对学习者来说没有正在使用的词缀，但古法语动词中的 re- 值得一提，它暗示「重新、换一套再做」。

latinIntro.en: Relay comes through French, not Latin, so the usual Latin relatives are weak; relaier itself traces back to Latin laxare, to loosen, which is only indirect evidence.
latinIntro.cn: relay 经法语而非拉丁语进入英语，常见的拉丁同族词并不扎实；relaier 本身可追溯到拉丁语 laxare（放松），但这只是旁证。

items.example: Re- hints at taking up the journey again.
items.exampleCN: re- 暗示重新接过行程。

items.example: Relai is the direct source of relay.
items.exampleCN: relai 是 relay 的直接来源。

items.meaning: to leave and replace with a new set
items.example: The verb lies behind the modern spelling.
items.exampleCN: 这一动词是今拼写的底层形式。

items.meaningCN: 过去式与过去分词词尾
items.example: Add -ed to get relayed.
items.exampleCN: 加 -ed 构成 relayed。

items.example: Relaying names the forwarding itself.
items.exampleCN: relaying 指中继转发这一动作。

items.example: Relays serves both as a verb and a noun.
items.exampleCN: relays 既作动词三单，也作名词复数。

items.example: Man combines with relay to make relayman.
items.exampleCN: man 与 relay 组合成 relayman。

items.meaning: a fixed point on a route
items.example: Relay station keeps the post-horse idea alive.
items.exampleCN: relay station 保留了驿马换站的旧画面。

latinEntries.example: Laxare is only an indirect root behind the French verb.
latinEntries.exampleCN: laxare 只是法语动词背后的间接词根。

definition_zh: 不懈的；无情的；持续不断的；毫不松懈的
definition_en: never stopping and never becoming gentler, whether describing effort, pressure, or a person who shows no mercy
core_image: 一块从不松劲的弓弦，越拉越紧，从不垂下
scene: 教练的质询一刻不停，让整个团队都喘不过气。The coaches asked relentless questions, and nobody in the team had time to relax.
sceneCN: 这里 relentless 是「不间断的」的意思（第 2 个义项：持续而不减弱）；句意：教练们提问毫不间断，队里没人有空歇口气。

pos.zh: 不懈的；无情的；持续不断的

derivatives.zh: relentless 去掉 -less 后的动词，义为「变缓和；发慈悲」
relentless 加 -ly，义为「不停地；无情地」
relentless 加 -ness，义为「不懈；冷酷」

senses.title: Showing no pity or mercy
senses.definition: refusing to be gentle or show mercy, even when another person suffers
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝表现温和或怜悯，即使他人正在受苦
senses.example: The relentless critic tore apart every idea in the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 那位毫不留情的批评者把计划里的每个想法都批得体无完肤。
senses.why: Latin lentus means slow and yielding, and to relent is to soften, so relentless is literally not able to soften, which is the face of someone who never shows mercy.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 lentus 意为迟缓、容易退让，动词 relent 就是「变软、松口」；因此 relentless 字面是「无法变软」，正是一个从不心软、毫不留情者的面孔。

senses.title: Never stopping or easing
senses.titleCN: 持续不断的；毫不减弱的
senses.definition: continuing without any pause or reduction in strength
senses.definitionCN: 不停地继续，强度也毫不减弱
senses.example: The relentless rain washed away the road.
senses.exampleCN: 不停歇的雨水把道路冲毁了。
senses.why: If the force never softens, it never lets up, so the same word easily describes rain, pressure, or noise that goes on without a break.
senses.whyCN: 一股力量既然从不变软，也就从不停歇；于是同一个词可以形容雨、压力或噪音，强调的正是「一直往上顶着、没有片刻放松」。

senses.title: Persisting with tireless effort
senses.definition: keeping on with determined effort although tired or opposed
senses.definitionCN: 即使疲惫或遭到阻力，仍以坚定的努力坚持做下去
senses.example: Her relentless practice finally won her a place on the team.
senses.exampleCN: 她不懈的练习终于让她赢得队里的一席之地。
senses.why: Something that will not soften also will not stop, so the word praises people whose effort simply refuses to let go.
senses.whyCN: 不会软化的东西同样不会停下；反过来用，这个词就成了褒义的赞语，形容努力的人一直抓着目标不松手，百折不挠。

senses.title: Pursued with no let-up
senses.definition: carried out with such persistence that the target is given no rest
senses.definitionCN: 以极强毅力进行，使被追赶的一方得不到喘息
senses.example: The detectives kept up a relentless search for the missing files.
senses.exampleCN: 警探们对失踪文件穷追不舍。
senses.why: A hunt that never relaxes its grip is both cruel and unstoppable, and this sense combines the no-pity and never-stop meanings.
senses.whyCN: 一场从不放松的追捕既显得不留情面，又显得停不下来；这一义项正是把「无情」与「不停」两层意思叠在一起，落在一个具体行动上。

senses.title: Refusing to change a course
senses.titleCN: 不可动摇的；固执到底的
senses.definition: not yielding to persuasion or change of direction
senses.definitionCN: 面对劝说或改变方向的要求仍不屈服
senses.example: His relentless insistence on the old timetable caused months of delay.
senses.exampleCN: 他坚持旧时间表一步不让，导致拖延了数月。
senses.why: To relent also means to give way, so one who will not relent stands fixed, and the word can almost mean stubborn rather than merciless.
senses.whyCN: relent 也有「让步」的意思，所以不 relent 的人就是站着不动；此时 relentless 已接近「固执」，描述的是不肯改变路线的态度。

intro.en: Relentless is relent plus the privative suffix -less, and relent comes from Latin lentus, slow or slack, itself probably from the root of lentis, the lentil, which a slow thing resembles.
intro.cn: relentless 由动词 relent 加表否定的词尾 -less 构成；relent 来自拉丁语 lentus（迟缓、松弛），一般认为该词根与 lentis（小扁豆）有关，取其形状缓慢摊开的意象。

items.en: Lentus means slow, tough, and pliant, so it can describe both a slow river and soft wax.
items.cn: lentus 意为迟缓、黏韧、柔软，既可以形容缓缓流动的河，也可以形容柔软的蜡。

items.en: The verb relentare grows out of lentus and carries the idea of becoming slack.
items.cn: 动词 relentare 由 lentus 派生，带有「变松弛」的意思。

items.en: To relent means to melt with pity or grow gentle, often describing a person who finally gives in.
items.cn: 中古英语 relent 表示「心生怜悯、变温和」，常形容人终于软下心来。

items.en: The adjective relentless appears as a plain negative, meaning unable to be softened.
items.cn: 形容词 relentless 出现，是直截了当的否定形式，意为「无法被软化」。

items.en: Writers extend it from human cruelty to rain, wind, pressure, and pursuit.
items.cn: 此后作家把它的用途从人的狠心扩展到雨、风、压力与追逐。

note.en: Relentless is built on relent, so it stands beside the same-root family and beside words for unending effort.
note.cn: relentless 建立在 relent 之上，因此形近组是它的同词族，意义组则是不停歇、不放弃一类的词。

entries.definition: to become gentler or accept that you were too harsh
entries.definitionCN: 变得缓和；松口让步

entries.definition: in a way that never stops or softens
entries.definitionCN: 不停地；毫不留情地

entries.definition: the quality of being connected to the matter in hand
entries.definitionCN: 相关性；切题。只是拼写开头相近，词源不同：relevance 来自 relevare。

entries.definition: impossible to stop or persuade
entries.definitionCN: 不可阻挡的；无法劝服的

entries.definition: continuing firmly in spite of difficulty
entries.definitionCN: 坚持不懈的；持续不断的

entries.definition: never stopping or weakening
entries.definitionCN: 从不间断的；不放松的

normalIntro.en: Relentless is relent with a minus sign: the softening never happens.
normalIntro.cn: relentless 就是给 relent 加一个减号：变软这件事永远不会发生。

normal.en: Relentless is relent plus -less, just as endless is end plus -less.
normal.cn: relentless 是 relent 加 -less，正如 endless 是 end 加 -less。

normal.en: The adverb is relentlessly, not relently, so keep the full stem and add -ly.
normal.cn: 副词是 relentlessly，而不是 relently，要保留完整的词干再加 -ly。

normal.en: To relent means to soften, so relentless people never soften.
normal.cn: relent 意为变软，所以 relentless 的人从不心软。

normal.en: Relentless pressure is pressure that never eases off.
normal.cn: relentless pressure 是丝毫不减的压力。

normal.en: Compare tireless: tireless praises effort, relentless often warns of something harsher.
normal.cn: 对比 tireless：tireless 多在称赞努力，relentless 往往带有一点厉害的意味。

abstract.en: Picture a bowstring drawn tight and never allowed to slacken.
abstract.cn: 想象一根弓弦被拉得紧紧的，从来不松。

abstract.en: See rain falling on the same road, day after day, with no break.
abstract.cn: 想象雨落在同一条路上，一天接一天，片刻不停。

abstract.en: Imagine a runner who keeps the same pace long after everyone else has stopped.
abstract.cn: 想象一名跑者，在所有人都停下之后仍保持原来的配速。

examples.en: The team made a relentless effort to finish the bridge before winter.
examples.cn: 团队为在冬天前修完这座桥而做出了不懈的努力。

examples.en: The relentless wind kept the boats in the harbour for three days.
examples.cn: 不停歇的狂风让船只三天都没能出海。

examples.en: She was relentless in her questions and refused every easy answer.
examples.cn: 她的追问毫不放松，拒绝接受任何敷衍的回答。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞兰勒斯」——想象一匹叫瑞兰的骏马，勒斯（勒住）也勒不住它，越跑越快、从不松劲，这就是 relentless 的不停不松；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 lentus（迟缓；柔软）→ 中世纪动词 relentare → 英语 relent（变软、让步）+ 否定词尾 -less → relentless（不会变软、不会停下的）。

sensesIntro.en: Relentless keeps one negative idea, never softening, and spreads it from a merciless person to unending forces, tireless effort, nonstop pursuit, and a course that will not change.
sensesIntro.cn: relentless 只守着一个否定意思「从不软化」，再由这层意思伸向无情的人、不停歇的力量、不懈的努力、穷追不舍的行动和不肯改变的路线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bowstring that is never allowed to slacken.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根始终不允许松下的弓弦。

branches.en: The missing softness shows first as hardness toward people.
branches.cn: 缺少的柔软首先表现为对人冷硬。

branches.en: A force that will not soften also will not break off.
branches.cn: 不会软化的力也不会断，于是成了不停歇。

branches.en: Turning the same refusal inward makes tireless effort.
branches.cn: 把同样的「不松口」用在自己身上，就成了不懈努力。

branches.en: Pursuit and refusal to yield are the no-mercy and no-stop senses aimed at one goal.
branches.cn: 穷追与坚持到底，正是无情与不停两层意思对准了同一个目标。

branches.en: Both share the idea that nothing is ever allowed to let up.
branches.cn: 两者共享同一点：从不允许有任何松动。

intro.en: Relentless is a verb stem plus a negative suffix, and further endings grow adverbs and nouns from it.
intro.cn: relentless 是动词词干加否定词尾，之后又能加副词与名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin lentus, slow or soft, gives the base, and in French it developed the sense of slackening and giving in.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 lentus 意为迟缓、柔软，提供词干基础，传入法语后发展出「松弛、让步」的意思。

items.example: Re- belongs to the older verb relent.
items.exampleCN: re- 属于较早的动词 relent。

items.example: Lent- carries the soft and slow image.
items.exampleCN: lent- 承载着柔软与迟缓的意象。

items.example: The suffix makes the negated adjective.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾构成否定形容词。

items.example: Add -ly to get the adverb.
items.exampleCN: 加 -ly 得到副词。

items.example: Add -ness to name the quality.
items.exampleCN: 加 -ness 命名这种性质。

items.example: Unrelenting is a close cousin of relentless.
items.exampleCN: unrelenting 是 relentless 的近亲。

items.example: Relenting names the very softening that stops.
items.exampleCN: relenting 指的正是那个会发生的软化。

items.example: Lentitude keeps the Latin root in plain sight.
items.exampleCN: lentitude 让拉丁词根清晰可见。

definition_zh: 相关性；切题；现实意义；关联性
definition_en: the quality of being closely connected with the subject, situation, or person at hand
core_image: 两支箭头正对着同一个靶点，说明这条信息落对了地方
scene: 老师问这篇新闻和今天的讨论有什么关系。The teacher asked what relevance the news had to our discussion today.
sceneCN: 这里 relevance 是「相关性」的意思（第 1 个义项：与当前议题的关联）；句意：老师问这条新闻和今天的讨论有什么关系。

derivatives.zh: relevance 去掉名词词尾 -ance 的形容词，义为「相关的；切题的」
relevant 加否定前缀 ir-，义为「无关的；不相干的」
irrelevant 的名词形式，义为「不相关；无关紧要」
relevance 的变体拼写，多见于法律文本，义同「相关性」

senses.title: Being connected to the issue at hand
senses.definition: the connection between a fact, idea, or answer and the matter being discussed
senses.definitionCN: 某个事实、想法或答案与正在讨论的事情之间的联系
senses.example: Judges ask whether every sentence has relevance to the main claim.
senses.exampleCN: 评判者会问每一句话是否都与中心论点相关。
senses.why: Latin relevare means to raise and lighten, and something relevant lifts itself up into the matter that matters, so relevance is the quality of standing in that same circle.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 relevare 意为「抬起、使轻松」，有关的事物就像被抬起、落进当前要处理的事情里；因此 relevance 指的是「站进同一个圈子里」的属性。

senses.title: Value for a real situation
senses.definition: the importance or usefulness that something has for real life now
senses.definitionCN: 某事物当下对现实生活的重要性或有用性
senses.example: The poem still has relevance for readers struggling with loss.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗对正经历失去之苦的读者仍有现实意义。
senses.why: If a thing is connected to what matters, it also helps with it, so relevance moves from being on topic to being worth something now.
senses.whyCN: 一件事既然与要紧的事相连，也就对它有推动；于是 relevance 从「话题上贴题」推进到「当下实实在在有用、有意义」。

senses.title: Topicality in the news
senses.definition: the quality of relating to events that are current or important to an audience
senses.definitionCN: 与当前发生的事件或受众关心的事情相关的性质
senses.example: The show lost ratings when it lost relevance to younger viewers.
senses.exampleCN: 这档节目失去与年轻观众的关联后就掉了收视。
senses.why: Media often measures connection to the present, so relevance becomes a kind of score for how well a message meets today.
senses.whyCN: 媒体常以「是否接得上当下」来衡量价值，relevance 于是变成一把尺子，衡量信息与今天的世界贴合得有多紧。

senses.title: Legal relevance of evidence
senses.definition: in law, the tendency of evidence to make a fact in dispute more or less probable
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上，证据使争议事实更可能或更不可能成立的程度
senses.example: The lawyer challenged the relevance of the old photographs.
senses.exampleCN: 律师质疑那些旧照片与案件证据的关联性。
senses.why: The plain idea of connection is tightened by the courts into a test, and the noun gains a technical legal sense.
senses.whyCN: 法院把「有联系」这一朴素观念收紧成一条标准，法官据此判断证据是否推向争点，名词也由此获得一个法律术语义。

senses.title: Search results matching a query
senses.titleCN: 检索结果与提问的匹配度
senses.definition: in computing, how well a result matches what a person actually asked for
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机检索中，结果与人真正询问的内容相匹配的程度
senses.example: Better relevance scores pushed useful pages to the top.
senses.exampleCN: 更好的相关度评分把有用的网页推到了前面。
senses.why: Search engines inherited the old question about connection and turned it into a number, so relevance now ranks answers as well as naming their link.
senses.whyCN: 搜索引擎继承了「有没有联系」这个老问题，并把它变成一个分数；如今 relevance 既能说明答案是否相关，也能用来给答案排序。

intro.en: Relevance comes from Latin relevare, to raise or lighten, through the adjective relevant, which once meant helping or relieving and later narrowed to being connected.
intro.cn: relevance 源自拉丁语 relevare（抬起、减轻），经形容词 relevant 传入英语；relevant 早期意为「有帮助、能缓解」，后来收窄为「有联系」。

items.en: Levare means to lighten, and levis means light in weight, so relevare is to lift a burden.
items.cn: levere 意为减轻，levis 意为轻的，因此 relevare 是把负担抬起来。

items.en: Relevare also serves in legal language for raising a matter before a court.
items.cn: 在中世纪拉丁语中，relevare 也用于法律语境，指把一桩事情提交法庭。

items.en: Relevant enters English meaning tending to help or relieve a case.
items.cn: relevant 进入英语时，意为「对案件有帮助、能减轻分量」。

items.en: The sense narrows from helping to bearing on the matter in hand.
items.cn: 此后词义从「有帮助」收窄为「与所议之事有关」。

items.en: The abstract noun relevance appears and is later taken up by education, the law, and computing.
items.cn: 抽象名词 relevance 出现，随后进入教育、法律与计算机领域。

note.en: Relevance is the noun of connection, so its look-alikes are the same root family and its neighbours are words for bearing on a question.
note.cn: relevance 是表示「有联系」的名词，形近组是同根词族，意义组则是围绕「与问题有关」的同义词。

entries.definition: closely connected with the subject
entries.definitionCN: 相关的；切题的

entries.definition: the state of being not connected with the subject
entries.definitionCN: 不相关；无关紧要

entries.definition: never stopping or becoming gentler
entries.definitionCN: 不懈的；无情的。只是拼写开头相近，词源不同：relentless 来自 lentus（柔软）。

entries.definition: the quality of relating directly to the matter
entries.definitionCN: （正式的）切题；贴切

entries.definition: the fact of being able to be used in a particular case
entries.definitionCN: 适用性；可应用性

entries.definition: the importance or meaning that something has
entries.definitionCN: 重要性；意义

normalIntro.en: Relevance is the noun behind relevant: a thing is relevant when it can be lifted up next to the matter.
normalIntro.cn: relevance 是 relevant 背后的名词：一件事能被提到当前议题旁边，它就 relevant。

normal.en: Relevant loses its final t to become relevance.
normal.cn: relevant 去掉词尾 t 再加 -ance，就变成 relevance。

normal.en: Have relevance to means to be connected with.
normal.cn: have relevance to 表示与某事物有关联。

normal.en: The opposite noun is irrelevance, from the prefix ir-.
normal.cn: 它的反义名词是 irrelevance，由否定前缀 ir- 构成。

normal.en: In computing, relevance ranks search results.
normal.cn: 在计算机领域，relevance 用来给搜索结果排序。

normal.en: Compare pertinence: pertinence is formal, relevance is the everyday word.
normal.cn: 对比 pertinence：pertinence 较正式，relevance 更常用。

abstract.en: Picture one arrow hitting the mark that the speaker was aiming at.
abstract.cn: 想象一支箭正好射中说话人瞄准的那个靶点。

abstract.en: See an old book found useful again by someone facing the same problem.
abstract.cn: 想象一本旧书，因为有人遇上同样的问题而再次变得有用。

abstract.en: Imagine a front page that changes its story whenever the world changes.
abstract.cn: 想象一张头版，世界一变，上面的报道就跟着换。

examples.en: The relevance of the study to local farming was clear at once.
examples.cn: 这项研究与当地农业的关联一望便知。

examples.en: Some old sayings have lost their relevance for young workers.
examples.cn: 有些老话对年轻工人已经失去了现实意义。

examples.en: The judge questioned the relevance of the letter to the case.
examples.cn: 法官质疑那封信与本案的关联性。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞乐文思」——瑞雪里快乐地文思涌动，讲的全是与题目紧密相关的事；这里的「文思」正提示「文章要相关」。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 levare（举起；使轻）← levis（轻的）→ relevare（抬起、减轻）→ 中世纪拉丁语 relevare（把事提到法庭）→ relevant → relevance，核心以「抬到当前议题旁边」为线索。

sensesIntro.en: Relevance begins as the relation between a point and the matter in hand, then becomes value for real life, fitness for the news, a legal test for evidence, and a score for search results.
sensesIntro.cn: relevance 先指某一点与当前议题之间的关系，再延伸为对现实生活的价值、与当下时事的贴合、证据的法律关联标准，以及检索结果的排序分数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow landing exactly on the point being discussed.
core.cn: 核心意象：箭正好落在正在讨论的那个点上。

branches.en: A point is relevant when it sits inside the circle of the question.
branches.cn: 一点只要落在问题的圈子里，就具备相关性。

branches.en: What matters now is what helps people now.
branches.cn: 当下有意义的东西，就是当下能帮人的东西。

branches.en: The press measures connection by today, not by history.
branches.cn: 媒体用今天而不是历史来衡量关联。

branches.en: Courts and computers both turn the connection into a formal test or score.
branches.cn: 法院与计算机都把这种联系转成正式的判断或分数。

branches.en: Being on topic and being useful are two steps of the same connection.
branches.cn: 贴题与有用是同一根联系上的两级台阶。

intro.en: Relevance is a Latin verb stem with an abstract noun ending, so it belongs to a family that runs from relieve to irrelevant.
intro.cn: relevance 是拉丁语动词词干加抽象名词词尾，所以它属于从 relieve 一路排到 irrelevant 的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin levare, from levis meaning light, gives lift and relief, and relevare means to raise up or ease.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 levare 来自 levis（轻的），意为举起、减轻，relevare 表抬起或缓解。

items.example: Re- adds the sense of lifting up again.
items.exampleCN: re- 加上再次抬起的意思。

items.example: Lev- appears in lever and levity.
items.exampleCN: lev- 出现在 lever 与 levity 中。

items.example: The ending forms relevant.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾构成 relevant。

items.example: Add -ance to make relevance.
items.exampleCN: 加 -ance 构成 relevance。

items.example: Relevancy is the variant spelling.
items.exampleCN: relevancy 是变体拼写。

items.example: Ir- before r gives irrelevant.
items.exampleCN: 在 r 前用 ir- 构成 irrelevant。

items.example: Relevantly appears in formal English.
items.exampleCN: relevantly 多出现在正式英语中。

items.example: Levis is the root behind levity too.
items.exampleCN: levis 也是 levity 的词根。

items.example: Levare lies inside relevare.
items.exampleCN: levare 嵌在 relevare 之中。

items.example: Relevare is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: relevare 是直接的拉丁来源。

definition_zh: 依靠；依赖；信赖；依靠的人或物
definition_en: the state of depending on someone or something, or the trust placed in it
core_image: 把身体的重量整个压在另一样东西上，松开便站不住
scene: 徒步者在迷雾中迷了路，只能紧紧依赖手里的指南针。Lost in thick fog, the hiker had to place complete reliance on her compass.
sceneCN: 这里 reliance 表示「依赖」（第 1 个义项：在需要时依靠某人或某物）；句意：徒步者在浓雾中迷了路，只能完全依赖手里的指南针。

pos.zh: 依靠；依赖；信赖；依靠的人或物

derivatives.zh: 动词原形，义为「依靠；信赖」
rely 加形容词后缀 -able，义为「可靠的；可信赖的」
reliable 加否定前缀 un-，义为「不可靠的」
reliable 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「可靠地」

senses.title: The act of depending on something
senses.definition: the state of needing someone or something in order to live, work, or succeed
senses.definitionCN: 为了生活、工作或成功而需要某人某物的状态
senses.example: The country has a heavy reliance on imported fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家严重依赖进口燃料。
senses.why: The verb rely came from Latin religare, to bind fast, so reliance is the picture of being tied to something that holds you up.
senses.whyCN: 动词 rely 源自拉丁语 religare（缚紧），所以 reliance 的画面是被某物牢牢系住、由它把你撑住。

senses.title: Trust placed in a person or thing
senses.definition: the confidence that someone or something will do what is needed
senses.definitionCN: 相信某人或某物会做到所需之事的信心
senses.example: The board placed reliance on his judgment.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会信赖他的判断。
senses.why: The same binding image can be read from the inside: if you are tied to something, you are also trusting it not to give way.
senses.whyCN: 同一条「系住」的意象也可以从内侧理解：既然被系在某个东西上，也就等于信它不会断掉。

senses.title: A person or thing that one leans on
senses.definition: someone or something that supports or helps a person in need
senses.definitionCN: 在困难时给予支撑或帮助的人或物
senses.example: She was the family main reliance during the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 危机期间她是一家人主要的依靠。
senses.why: When the abstract dependence is turned back into a concrete noun, the thing you lean on becomes a reliance itself.
senses.whyCN: 当抽象的依赖被还原为一个具体名词时，被你靠着的那根「柱子」本身也成了 reliance。

senses.title: Dependence in a serious legal matter
senses.definition: the legal ground of relying on a rule, promise, or fact when a claim is made
senses.definitionCN: 提出主张时对规则、承诺或事实的合法依赖作为依据
senses.example: The claim rests on reliance on the written contract.
senses.exampleCN: 该主张以对书面合同的依赖为依据。
senses.why: Legal writing keeps the plain sense of depending on something, but narrows the tie to rights and obligations.
senses.whyCN: 法律文本保留了「依赖某物」的普通含义，只把这种关系收窄到权利义务上。

senses.title: Dependence on drugs or alcohol
senses.definition: a medical condition in which a person depends on a substance and cannot easily give it up
senses.definitionCN: 医学上指对某种物质产生依赖、难以戒断的状况
senses.example: Treatment aims to reduce reliance on painkillers.
senses.exampleCN: 治疗目标是减少对止痛药的依赖。
senses.why: Medical use takes the physical lean and applies it to the body, which has learned to lean on a substance.
senses.whyCN: 医学用法把身体的「倚靠」挪到生理层面：身体已经学会靠某样物质才能维持运转。

senses.title: Over-dependence that makes a flaw dangerous
senses.titleCN: 单点故障；过度依赖造成的隐患
senses.definition: engineering term for a system failure that can be traced to one single point of dependence
senses.definitionCN: 工程术语，指可追溯到单一依赖点的系统故障
senses.example: Engineers found a single point of reliance in the backup system.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在备份系统中发现了一处单点依赖。
senses.why: In engineering the word singles out the one joint every load passes through, so reliance changes from strength into hidden risk.
senses.whyCN: 在工程语境里，这个词专指所有负荷都要经过的那个接点，于是「依赖」从支柱变成了潜藏风险。

senses.title: Confidence that a device will work
senses.definition: the degree to which users can trust equipment or software to perform correctly
senses.definitionCN: 使用者对设备或软件能正确运行的信任程度
senses.example: Passengers show high reliance on automated braking.
senses.exampleCN: 乘客对自动刹车系统表现出很高的信赖。
senses.why: When machines take over tasks, the trust that people used to place in each other is transferred to the equipment.
senses.whyCN: 当机器接管任务时，人们原本彼此之间托付的信赖就转移到了设备上。

senses.title: Relying on one another as a social value
senses.definition: the mutual dependence of groups or nations on each other for goods and support
senses.definitionCN: 群体或国家之间在物资与支持上的相互依赖
senses.example: Global trade creates mutual reliance between distant economies.
senses.exampleCN: 全球贸易使相隔遥远的经济体相互依赖。
senses.why: If one person can lean on another, whole societies can be pictured leaning on each other in a net of trade.
senses.whyCN: 若一个人可以靠着另一个人，那么整个社会就能被想象成一张彼此依靠的贸易之网。

intro.en: Reliance is the noun of rely, which was borrowed from Old French and goes back to the Latin verb religare, to bind fast.
intro.cn: reliance 是 rely 的名词形式，经由古法语借入，可追溯到拉丁语动词 religare（缚紧）。

items.en: Religare, to bind back or bind fast, is the base verb, so the root image is something held by a cord.
items.cn: religare（重新系上、缚紧）是基础动词，词根意象是被绳索缚住的东西。

items.en: The verb religare is tied to religio, an obligation binding a person, though the family may also involve re-ligere, to reread.
items.cn: 动词 religare 与 religio（约束人的义务）相关，但这一词族也可能涉及 re-ligere（重新阅读），两种解释并存。

items.en: Old French relied, to gather or tie together, made the linkage of ideas concrete.
items.cn: 古法语 relied（把东西收拢、系在一起）使「联结想法」的过程具体可见。

items.en: English rely first meant to join or attach oneself to something, and only later to trust it.
items.cn: 英语 rely 最初意为「使自己依附于某物」，后来才引申为「信赖」。

items.en: The noun reliance appears and settles the abstract sense of trusting or depending.
items.cn: 名词 reliance 出现，确立了「信赖、依靠」的抽象含义。

items.en: Modern usage adds medical, engineering, and economic uses of reliance.
items.cn: 现代用法扩展出医学、工程与经济领域中的「依赖」含义。

note.en: Reliance sits with rely, reliance, or a reliability family, and its near meanings are dependence, trust, and faith.
note.cn: reliance 与 rely、reliably 等词构成词族，近义地位则与 dependence、trust、faith 相邻。
